blocks.markdown: Secs. 81–82 impose **relationship-disclosure requirements**. The point is to make **relevant relationships transparent** and protect procurement integrity. For a scenario, identify **the person/entity required to disclose, what relationship is covered, when disclosure is made, and the consequence** under the statute/IRR.

When discussing **protests or dispute resolution**, specify the **stage, available administrative mechanism, filing deadline and prerequisites**. A "protest" is **not a generic objection that can be filed at any time**. Do not conflate a procurement protest with **judicial review, civil liability, administrative discipline or criminal liability**; these can coexist but have distinct elements and procedures.

Identify whether the respondent is a **bidder/supplier/contractor or a public officer**, the **prohibited conduct**, the **governing authority**, **due-process step**, **length/scope of sanction**, and **appeal or reinstatement mechanism**. Use the **current IRR** for the exact grounds and sanction procedure.

**Three separations to keep straight:**

- Separate **bidder disqualification for a specific procurement** from **suspension or blacklisting** affecting future opportunities.
- Separate **administrative consequences** from **penalties under other laws**.
- Grounds must be tied to **evidence and the statutory category**; poor performance, material misrepresentation, collusion, abandonment or other conduct may have different procedures and consequences under applicable rules.

description: Relationship disclosures, protests and disputes, and the suspension, blacklisting, and sanctions regime.
title: Disclosure and sanctions
